papers.title: Spectroscopy-informed Deep Learning Searches for Photometric Little Red Dots in JWST Surveys
papers.abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are a population of compact, red sources discovered at high redshift with JWST that exhibit distinctive V-shaped spectral energy distributions (SEDs). Existing LRD samples are typically identified using a variety of color-based selection criteria, which can lead to differences in the populations recovered by different studies. We develop a cross-modal machine-learning framework that combines matched NIRCam imaging and NIRSpec/PRISM spectroscopy to transfer spectroscopic information into imaging-based representations, enabling LRD identification from JWST/NIRCam imaging alone. Applied to spectroscopically observed high-redshift galaxies previously classified as non-LRDs, our model identifies 35 new LRD candidates. The majority satisfy at least one independent LRD color selection criterion, and among the 13 candidates with medium- or high-resolution NIRSpec grating spectra, 10 exhibit broad H$α$ emission - a hallmark of LRDs. We further apply the classifier to public NIRCam imaging from the Dawn JWST Archive and two independent JWST surveys, yielding 357 and 23 additional LRD candidates, respectively. The candidates recovered by our method span a broader range of observed SED properties than those in existing samples, suggesting that current color-selected samples may not fully capture the diversity of LRD-like systems present in JWST surveys. Our findings highlight the value of spectroscopy-informed photometric classification as a powerful strategy for systematically mining large-area JWST imaging datasets and provide a practical framework for future studies of this emerging population.

papers.title: Magnetic Properties of Galactic Molecular Clouds
papers.abstract: The earliest studies of molecular clouds (MCs) showed scaling relations between mass and radius M$\sim$R^s with exponent s $\approx$ 2, known as the third Larson relation. More recent CO surveys indicate 2 < s < 3 in the inner Milky Way (MW) and nearby galaxies. These observations appear consistent with the virial equilibrium (VE) of magnetically subcritical clouds, bound by the pressure Pe of the midplane ISM. The VE equations for such clouds are consistent with 2 < s < 3 for magnetically subcritical clouds, but not for magnetically critical, supercritical, or nonmagnetic clouds. We fit the subcritical VE equations to M-R trends observed in CO surveys of $\sim$1500 clouds, with correlation coefficients 0.8 - 1. The fits indicate median mass-to-flux ratio lambda $\approx$ 0.7, magnetic field strength Btot $\approx$ 60$\mathrm{μG}$, and Pe/k $\approx$ 5 x 10^5 cm^-3 K in the inner MW, with lesser values in M33 and M31. For 18 MW "bones," VE analysis assuming likely values of Pe also indicates subcritical values of lambda, as found from polarization observations. These results indicate that many giant molecular clouds (GMCs) are consistent with pressure-bound magnetically subcritical virial equilibrium. If so, GMCs may have low star formation efficiency (SFE) because their relatively strong fields cause filaments, clumps and cores to form slowly, while feedback and turbulence disperse them rapidly. The fields in their clumps and cores are likely weak enough to allow star-forming collapse, according to Zeeman and DCF observations, and according to MHD simulations which predict SFE $\approx$ 0.5-2%.

papers.title: Population synthesis of substellar companions surviving common-envelope evolution
papers.abstract: Predicting the population of substellar companions around white dwarfs (WDs) requires accounting for both companions that avoid engulfment during stellar evolution and those that survive common-envelope (CE) evolution. While the former population was investigated in our previous population-synthesis study, a comprehensive population synthesis of the latter remains lacking. We investigated the fate of engulfed substellar companions within the same population-synthesis framework. We aim to predict the occurrence rates and properties of companions surviving CE evolution, identify the conditions permitting survival, and assess their detectability. We determined the stellar structure at the onset of CE evolution and calculated CE outcomes for different ejection efficiencies considering gravitational and thermal energy or the full internal energy of the envelope. Survival is rare and strongly depends on the evolutionary stage at engulfment. No companions entering CE evolution during the red-giant branch or early asymptotic-giant branch survive. Survivors originate exclusively from the thermally pulsing asymptotic-giant branch, when stellar envelopes can become weakly bound, allowing even relatively low-mass companions to survive. The resulting systems typically have orbital periods of a few hours. We predict occurrence rates of up to 0.16% among WDs, corresponding to an upper limit of 2.53 companions to WDs within 50 pc. Transit detection is primarily limited by orbital geometry, whereas all predicted survivors would produce detectable infrared excess with JWST out to 50pc. We predict that CE evolution produces a small but observable population of close substellar companions to WDs. Survival is governed not only by companion mass but critically by the envelope structure at engulfment, particularly during thermal pulses, and by the contribution of recombination energy to envelope ejection.

papers.title: Adaptive Optics for the Extremely Large Telescope: overcoming Point Spread Function challenges with MORFEO
papers.abstract: MORFEO is the multi-conjugate adaptive optics (MCAO) relay for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) of the European Southern Observatory. It combines the adaptive mirrors of the telescope (M4-M5) with two post-focal deformable mirrors to deliver a stable, diffraction-limited point spread function over a field approaching 1'. MORFEO senses the atmosphere using six sodium laser guide stars and up to three natural guide stars distributed across a $\sim$160'' technical field, enabling sky coverage levels of order 50% at the South Galactic Pole. Through its two gravity-invariant ports, MORFEO feeds the MICADO first-light imager and spectrograph with a corrected field of 51''and HARMONI, the high-angular resolution integral field spectrograph. SHARP, a concept for a multi-object near-infrared spectrograph at the ELT, adopts MORFEO as its reference MCAO architecture for evaluating achievable image quality and scientific performance. In this paper, we summarise the MCAO capabilities delivered by MORFEO, its optical quality, tomographic performance, stability of the corrected focal plane, and the accuracy of telemetry-based PSF reconstruction, and discuss their relevance for the development of SHARP and other wide-field spectroscopic concepts at the ELT.

papers.title: From Early Concepts to Lunar Hypertelescopes Roadmap for Next-Generation Optical Astronomy on the Moon
papers.abstract: Since the dawn of the Space Age, the Moon has been considered one of the most promising locations for astronomical observations. The absence of atmosphere, exceptional mechanical stability, access to the permanently shielded radio-quiet far side, and the possibility of constructing extremely large apertures have motivated numerous concepts for lunar observatories over the past six decades. Despite extensive studies conducted during the Apollo era, most proposed lunar astronomy projects remained unrealized due to technological limitations, shifting scientific priorities, and the high cost of sustained lunar operations. Today, renewed international interest in lunar exploration, combined with advances in robotics, autonomous systems, additive manufacturing, precision optics, and formation flying, is reopening the prospect of large-scale astronomical infrastructures on the Moon. In particular, lunar hypertelescope concepts offer the possibility of achieving unprecedented angular resolutions through diluted optical arrays spanning hundreds of meters to several kilometres. This paper reviews the historical evolution of lunar astronomy concepts, analyses the reasons behind previous failures, examines current technological developments, and proposes a roadmap toward future lunar hypertelescope facilities capable of transforming observational astronomy during the twenty-first century.

papers.title: She Sees Shells by the Stellar Shore: A Kinematic View of NGC 253's Stellar Halo
papers.abstract: The stellar halos of nearby galaxies are fossil records of ancient mergers, providing insight into the formation and growth of these systems. These halos often contain substructure in the form of streams, shells, and debris fields that make up dynamically young remnants of past accretions. These remnants can be probed with resolved-star spectroscopic observations, giving insight into the kinematics of bygone satellite companions. Such observations have been made for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda, but are much more challenging and expensive to do outside the Local Group. The Local Volume has an abundance of MW-mass galaxies with richly structured halos, such as NGC 253. Leveraging the power of Magellan's M2FS fiber-fed multiobject spectrograph, we have obtained medium-resolution spectra of 225 stars centered on NGC 253's southwestern shell. These spectra enabled us to make the first-ever measurement of the resolved-star stellar kinematics for 89 stars in NGC 253's halo. We also detect substructure in several ways and identify regions likely to be accreted and in-situ, finding among them a low-velocity region coincident with the previously reported SW shell we believe was accreted recently, and an in-situ component that traces the outer disk. After subtracting NGC 253's systemic velocity, we measure median line-of-sight velocities of $-34_{-12}^{+16}$ km/s and $167_{-14}^{+16}$ km/s for the accreted and in-situ populations, respectively. This work highlights the utility of kinematics to differentiate between accreted and in-situ stars, and acts as a pathfinder for future observations with next-generation 30 m telescopes and wide-field multiobject spectrographs.

papers.title: Constraining the white-dwarf mass in the intermediate polar IGR J17014-4306 using X-ray and optical spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Intermediate polars (IPs), a subclass of magnetic cataclysmic variables, often show discrepancies between white-dwarf (WD) mass measurements from X-ray spectral modeling and optical dynamical studies. We investigate the IP IGR J17014-4306. We performed a joint spectral analysis of NuSTAR observations combined with archival XMM-Newton and Swift data, modeling the broad-band X-ray spectrum with a multi-temperature cooling-flow model. Additionally, we obtained time-resolved optical spectroscopy with the SOAR telescope to measure the radial velocity of the donor star and constrain the system's orbital parameters. The X-ray spectral analysis reveals a very high post-shock plasma temperature of $kT_{\max}=50_{-8}^{+11}\,\mathrm{keV}$, corresponding to a WD mass of $M_{\mathrm{WD}}=0.94_{-0.07}^{+0.09}\,M_\odot$. We also fitted the NuSTAR spectrum above 10 keV with the ipolar30KK model, obtaining $M_{\mathrm{WD}}=0.88_{-0.12}^{+0.14}\,M_\odot$. Our optical spectroscopy yields a radial-velocity semi-amplitude for the companion star of $K_2=165\pm4\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and an optical mass function of $f(M)=0.249\pm0.018\,M_\odot$. Combined with the eclipse geometry and the WD mass estimate from the X-ray models, these results favor a high mass ratio, $0.76\lesssim q\lesssim0.95$, and a donor-star mass of approximately $0.67\lesssim M_2/M_\odot\lesssim0.89$. In the limiting case of $q=1$, the WD mass has an upper limit of $1.14\,M_\odot$. Together with the X-ray measurements, this indicates a relatively massive WD. The lack of an independent measurement of the WD dynamical mass leaves it unclear whether the dynamical mass is consistent with the X-ray measurements or whether the X-ray mass is underestimated, as has been found for other IPs. Thus, our constraints make IGR J17014-4306 an important system for improving our understanding of IPs.

papers.title: From Earth's Harshest Landscapes to Lunar Horizons: Engineering NEA Telescopes for Extreme Environments
papers.abstract: Near-Earth Asteroids (NEAs) represent both a scientific opportunity and a potential threat to human civilization. While current survey programs have successfully detected most large NEAs, a significant observational gap remains for objects smaller than approximately 140 m, which can still produce regional-scale devastation. Ground-based surveys are intrinsically limited by atmospheric conditions, weather, and solar avoidance constraints, which leave a significant fraction of near-Sun objects difficult to detect. In particular, Earth-based observatories remain largely blind to objects approaching from the Sun-ward direction, reducing available warning times. Future lunar observatories offer a promising solution to this limitation. A telescope operating on the Moon could enable observations of regions inaccessible from Earth, provide enhanced sensitivity, and significantly improve early detection capabilities. However, the lunar environment imposes severe engineering constraints, including thermal cycling, dust contamination, radiation exposure, and autonomous operation requirements. We propose the AMAS(Atacama-Mongolia-Antarctica-Sahara) project, an international initiative using Earth's most extreme environments as analogue sites for future lunar astronomical facilities. By deploying and testing specialized NEA survey telescopes in these environments, key technologies for future lunar observatories can be validated under realistic operational conditions. This paper presents the scientific rationale, engineering challenges, site selection strategy, and long-term roadmap toward a global Earth-Moon network for planetary defense.

papers.title: Satisfying Freed--Witten quantization on smooth divisors in Calabi--Yau orientifolds
papers.abstract: Freed--Witten quantization conditions on several divisors wrapped by D-branes must be satisfied with one bulk $B$-field. On a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold $X$ with a holomorphic O3/O7 involution $σ$, we show that the common background $B_{2,+}^{\star}=\tfrac12[R]$, where $R$ is the total O7 divisor, permits Freed--Witten period quantization on the full two-cycle lattice of \emph{every smooth connected divisor}, modulo torsion. The worldvolume fluxes are chosen individually and obey the orientifold relation between each divisor and its image. The central step concerns setwise invariant divisors $D$: we prove that the bulk Freed--Witten class $η_D^\star=\tfrac12([R]+[D])|_D$ has integer periods on every $σ$-even integral two-cycle class, including inherited and autochthonous classes. Its periods on purely $σ$-odd classes vanish, so any remaining non-integer periods occur only on classes that are neither $σ$-even nor $σ$-odd. We show how to choose $σ$-odd worldvolume fluxes on these invariant divisors that make all periods integral. For exchanged divisor pairs, quantizing the flux on one member automatically quantizes its orientifold image. On invariant divisors with $h^{2,0}_-(D)=0$, the constructed flux is of type $(1,1)$ and admits a primitive representative; this includes every smooth rigid invariant divisor. We also study zero worldvolume flux on invariant divisors. For $h^{1,1}_-(X)\leq1$, we construct common bulk backgrounds satisfying every inherited intersection period on all such divisors. A binary compatibility test determines whether a common shift exists for larger $h^{1,1}_-(X)$. Non-inherited period tests then determine whether the resulting backgrounds allow zero flux on the full worldvolume lattices.

papers.title: How fast is the fastest-rotating O-type star in the Galaxy?
papers.abstract: {Rapid rotation distorts massive stars, making parameters from spherical models inclination-dependent. We studied these effects in the extreme Galactic O-type runaway LAMOST J040643.69+542347.8.} {We re-determined its stellar and rotational parameters with an oblate, gravity-darkened photospheric model and tabulated Stark profiles for selected \ion{He}{ii} lines.} {We fitted continuum-normalised spectra over 4000--4600\,Å with \texttt{ZPEKTR}, using TLUSTY/SYNSPEC emergent fluxes, limb darkening to weight their angular contribution over the visible Roche surface, Espinosa-Lara \& Rieutord gravity darkening, and Schöning--Butler Stark profiles. Its proximity to critical rotation should be assessed using $Ω/Ω_{\rm c}$, $v_{\rm e}/v_{\rm c}$, and $η_{\rm e}$ together. A controlled spherical fit with the same atmosphere grid is needed to isolate the bias from neglecting deformation and gravity darkening.}

papers.title: A distribution-function estimate of the Milky Way mass profile from outer halo stars in DESI DR2
papers.abstract: We present measurements of the Milky Way mass using blue horizontal-branch (BHB) and RR Lyrae (RRL) stars from the second data release of DESI (DR2), covering its first three years of operations. We employ 279 BHBs and 213 RRLs at $\sim\!50$--$80$\,kpc from the Galactic center, selected from catalogs roughly twice as large as those of DESI DR1, used in our previous mass measurement. We apply the Galactic Mass Estimator (GME), a hierarchical Bayesian framework that assumes power-law forms for the potential and the tracer density, and accounts for distance and velocity uncertainties. Validating the method on 24 AuriDESI mock catalogs (six Auriga halos at four viewing angles), we find that it overestimates the enclosed mass by $\sim\!15\%$ at 80\,kpc, and correct our results accordingly. We obtain $M(<80\,{\rm kpc}) = 0.64^{+0.06}_{-0.06}$ and $0.53^{+0.05}_{-0.05} \times 10^{12}\,M_\odot$ for BHBs and RRLs, respectively, while including Sagittarius stream stars lowers these masses by $\sim\!10$\%. Extrapolating to 100\,kpc, we obtain $M(<100\,{\rm kpc}) = 0.74^{+0.07}_{-0.07}$ and $0.62^{+0.06}_{-0.07} \times 10^{12}\,M_\odot$, and anchoring an NFW halo to our GME constraints at 65\,kpc yields virial masses of $M_{200} = 1.12^{+0.14}_{-0.12}$ and $0.89^{+0.11}_{-0.10} \times 10^{12}\,M_\odot$. BHBs yield systematically higher masses than RRLs across the full radial range, reflecting the impact of tracer choice even within a single method. This work is part of a wider DESI DR2 Key Project effort to measure the Milky Way mass and constrain systematics arising from different samples and methodologies.

papers.title: The impact of M dwarf stellar convection on exoplanetary atmospheric signatures. A 3D radiation-hydrodynamics simulation analysis for high-resolution spectroscopy
papers.abstract: M dwarf stars represent prime targets for the detection and characterization of small, temperate exoplanets; however, their complex activity and convective surfaces pose significant challenges for high-resolution spectroscopic studies. This work aims to investigate the impact of stellar convection on high-resolution spectroscopic observations of M dwarf stars and develop an integrated approach combining 3D radiative hydrodynamical simulations, spectroscopic modeling, and transit analysis to mitigate stellar noise. We employ 3D radiative hydrodynamical simulations of M dwarf stellar convection to generate synthetic spectra. We compare the synthetic spectra to actual observations of GJ 3470. We model a high-resolution transit sequence of the Neptune-size GJ 3470 b, including centre-to-limb variations (CLVs) and the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect (RME), and process the sequence via principal component analysis (PCA) to de-trend stellar effects. Comparison of synthetic spectra with actual observations shows that current H2O line lists remain inaccurate, with modest agreement in line strength and position for the chosen K-band interval. During the transit of GJ 3470 b, the amplitude of CLVs+RME is comparable to exoplanet signals. Current PCA can in principle de-trend such effects, but its behaviour is highly dependent on the copresence of telluric and planetary signals. While we are able to correctly detect the exoplanet with no evident bias from stellar residuals, this result is limited to a narrow spectral interval and a specific orbital configuration. This study demonstrates that 3D radiative hydrodynamical simulations are essential for accurately modeling convection-induced spectral variability in M dwarfs. Our integrated framework establishes a foundation to obtain unbiased measurements from future ELT observations of exoplanets orbiting M dwarfs.

papers.title: The spatial structure of solar magnetoconvection at scales up to $60$~Mm
papers.abstract: While convective motions at the scale of granules on the solar surface are well understood, those of mesogranular and supergranulation are not. At still larger scales, the lack of giant cells is a major mystery. We aim to slightly improve understanding of the radial and horizontal flows associated at mesogranular scales and supergranulation. We perform a deep MURaM small-scale dynamo simulation, extending from $50$~Mm below the solar surface and with a horizontal size of 60~Mm and sufficient resolution to begin to properly resolve the magnetic bright points in intergranular lanes. We determine the structure of the convective modes from the simulations at different scales, and compare the power spectra to those which have been previously observed. At all scales which are resolved by the simulation the simulated flows agree with the amplitude implied by Doppler measurements and local correlation tracking (LCT) measurements. The power in the vertical Doppler velocities at supergranular and larger scales is shown to be influenced by density perturbations near the surface. The structure of the modes at depth is simple as expected from the previous study of \cite{LordCameron2014} except the horizontal forcing scale scales like $H_ρ^{2/3}$ instead of $Hρ$. The simulations reproduce the observations up to scales of $60$~Mm. Within the simulated range, $l>=70$, we do not see the excess power associated with the convective conundrum.

papers.title: Photometric Study of a Distant SU UMa-type Dwarf Nova KSP-OT-201803a
papers.abstract: We present the discovery and photometric study of a distant dwarf nova KSP-OT-201803a using BVI-band observation data obtained by using the KMTNet Supernova Program. One superoutburst (SO) and three normal outbursts are identified from two years of observations (2018-2019), which show that KSP-OT-201803a is an SU UMa-type dwarf nova (DN). Applying the phase dispersion minimization method to the superhump data during the plateau phase of the SO yields a superhump period of P_sh = 127.4 minutes (=2.123 hr =0.08847 days). By stacking ten images of the quiescent phase, we find the quiescent phase magnitude of V = 22.59 +/- 0.18 mag. The SO shows quiescent-to-peak amplitude of 4.97 +/- 0.18 mag and duration of 16.59 days which are typical for the SU UMa-type DNe. Using the superhump period-orbital period relation of SU UMa stars, we obtain the approximate distance of 3.7 +/- 0.3 kpc to KSP-OT-201803a and Galactocentric distance of 9.4 kpc and height from the Galactic plane of +1.2 kpc. Stars at these large distances may belong to the Galactic halo or thick disk, which contain old, metal-poor Population II stars; therefore, these systems may have undergone a different evolutionary process than Population I objects. The orbital period gap of DNe spans 2.45-3.18 hours. Assuming that the orbital period of KSP-OT-201803a is a few percent shorter than its superhump period, KSP-OT-201803a may have just emerged from the period gap and recently resumed mass transfer after crossing its lower boundary.

papers.title: HLA-Net: A Physics-Guided Skeleton-Based Framework for Automatic Gravitational Arc Detection in Astronomical Images
papers.abstract: Gravitational arcs produced by strong gravitational lensing provide a unique approach for investigating dark matter distribution, galaxy cluster mass reconstruction and the structure of the Universe. Automated detection remains challenging because gravitational arcs are rare, often faint and morphologically similar to elongated galaxies.In this paper, we propose \textbf{HLA-Net (Hybrid Lens Arc Network)}, an interpretable multi-stage framework for automatic gravitational arc detection that explicitly exploits both the geometric morphology and physical characteristics of gravitational lensing without requiring manually annotated training datasets.The proposed framework was evaluated on astronomical FITS images containing complex galaxy cluster structures. Starting from 169 initial arc candidates extracted from ordered skeleton representations, the multi-stage verification pipeline reduced the search space to 83 geometrically consistent candidates, while robust circle fitting successfully modelled 113 candidate arc structures. The results demonstrate that HLA-Net effectively suppresses false-positive detections while preserving physically reasonable lens candidates through an interpretable and modular verification strategy.

papers.title: Quantum field theory treatment of the spin-flavor precession of Dirac neutrinos with diagonal magnetic moments
papers.abstract: We apply the quantum field theory (QFT) approach to describe the spin-flavor precession of Dirac neutrinos. The magnetic moments matrix of these neutrinos is taken to be diagonal in the mass basis. Neutrino mass eigenstates are considered to be virtual particles in the QFT approach. The neutrino contribution to the matrix element of the overall process, which includes the emission, the propagation and the detection of neutrinos, is contained in the propagators of massive neutrinos. Using the recently derived propagator of a massive neutrino, which exactly accounts for the magnetic moment interaction, we derive the transition probability of the process $ν_{e\mathrm{L}}\toν_{μ\mathrm{L}}$ under the influence of a magnetic field. The result is compared with the prediction of the standard quantum mechanical (QM) approach. We briefly discuss the possibility to derive the QFT corrections to the QM expressions.

papers.title: CHEX-MATE: Density profile reconstruction in galaxy clusters
papers.abstract: We investigated the reconstruction of the intra-cluster medium radial density profiles in galaxy clusters, focusing on the impact of cluster morphology, dynamical state, and methodological choices, within the framework of the CHEX-MATE project. Using a sample of 109 simulated galaxy clusters analysed along 40 independent lines of sight, we compared azimuthal mean and median techniques for deprojection. We find that azimuthal median-based density profiles recover the true gas density with negligible bias over the radial range $[0.15-1.3] R_{500}$. Mean based profiles are affected by the presence of substructures. While an accurate masking of clumps or substructures can reduce the bias to $< 5\%$, the discrepancy increases substantially in disturbed systems or when substructures remain unresolved. The mean-to-median density ratio statistically traces projected gas inhomogeneities, although intrinsic scatter and projection effects limit its use for individual clusters. The complementary use of mean and median profiles therefore provides the most complete approach for large X-ray cluster samples.

papers.title: Pushing the frontiers of low-frequency radio astronomy: An ultra-deep sub-arcsecond LOFAR image of ELAIS-N1
authors: J. M. G. H. J. de Jong
papers.abstract: We present ultra-deep sub-arcsecond radio images of the ELAIS-N1 field covering 2.5x2.5 deg^2, produced from 200 hours of LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR) observations in the 115-168 MHz band. The radio continuum images are obtained using recent advances in LOFAR long-baseline calibration and imaging. We achieve a central point-source sensitivity of 5.3 $μ$Jy/beam at an angular resolution of 0.33"x0.39" and an area-weighted sensitivity of 7.4 $μ$Jy/beam at 0.36"x0.45", making these the deepest radio images below 1.28 GHz to date and among the deepest at any radio frequency. By combining our data with previously released deep 6" LOFAR images, we compile a catalogue with a total of 62,916 unique radio sources across 2.5x2.5 deg^2. Our calibration strategy, combined with astrometric alignment using 95 Gaia quasars, results in positional offsets of $Δ$RA = -3 $\pm$ 27 mas and $Δ$DEC = 2 $\pm$ 17 mas for these same sources. We further demonstrate the potential for deep polarisation studies at sub-arcsecond resolution with instrumental leakages from Stokes I into linear polarisation down to 0.12%, which is about a factor of two better than the typical leakage in the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey at 6" resolution. Our results demonstrate that imaging a large number of observations over a wide field area at sub-arcsecond resolution is now computationally feasible. This establishes a new benchmark for low-frequency radio imaging in terms of combining depth, resolution, and survey area, which lays the foundation for deeper and wider surveys in the LOFAR2.0 and SKA era.

papers.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
papers.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field insensitivity.

papers.title: Spectroscopic diagnostics of coronal fan loops using EIS/Hinode and AIA/SDO
papers.abstract: We utilize spectroscopic and imaging data from the EIS/Hinode and the AIA/SDO to determine plasma and wave parameters along coronal fan loops. We determined the temperature along the loop lengths using the EM-loci method with EIS spectral lines and identified multi-thermal plasma components at temperatures ranging from 0.8-1.05, 1.2-1.4, and 1.6-1.8 MK. We further compared these temperature distributions along the loops with those derived from DEM analysis carried out using AIA coronal passbands. The multi-thermal nature of coronal fan loops can be well resolved using EIS spectroscopic data. We determined the density along the loop using the line-ratio method from the EIS Fe XII line pair. We found that density decreases slowly from the expected hydrostatic equilibrium. Our results demonstrate the multi-thermal nature of overdense loops, which can be well resolved with EIS spectroscopic data. We also determined the velocity amplitude of Alfvén waves from the non-thermal broadening of EIS Fe XII spectral line profiles. We further estimated the Alfvén wave energy flux in the corona by combining these parameters with the recently reported magnetic field strength of $\approx$200 G at the coronal footpoint of fan loops. The estimated Alfvén wave energy flux is $\approx$ 2$\times 10^7$ erg cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, significantly higher than those reported in earlier studies, and can contribute to coronal losses due to radiation along the fan loops in the active region.

papers.title: The PAU Survey: Self-supervised image denoising for flux-preserving photometry
papers.abstract: Context. Deep photometric surveys increasingly rely on low signal-to-noise imaging, where noise affects source detection, flux measurements, photometric redshifts, and sample selection. Self-supervised denoising methods are attractive because they do not require ground-truth images, but applying them to quantitative photometry requires controlling the flux biases they may introduce. Aims. We evaluate and improve Noise2Void (N2V) for denoising real astronomical images, focusing on preserving fluxes, reducing photometric scatter, and retaining the main source features across a wide magnitude range. Methods. We use real observations from the Physics of the Accelerating Universe Survey (PAUS) together with PAUS-like simulated images. We show that standard N2V systematically underestimates galaxy fluxes, especially for faint galaxies. To mitigate this bias, we add a bounded-output layer that limits large negative outputs, and fine-tune the model with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and two flux-aware loss terms that preserve the flux scale and improve repeated-exposure flux consistency. Results. For PAUS galaxies with 22 <= i_AB < 23 in the NB645 band, the standard N2V flux-ratio distribution peaks far below unity, while the bounded-output model restores it close to the original PAUS flux scale. The flux-aware LoRA fine-tuning reduces the width of the repeated-exposure flux-difference distribution to sigma_68 = 0.529 in NB645, an effective 47% reduction in random flux scatter relative to the original PAUS uncertainty scale, while keeping the median flux ratio close to unity. Conclusions. Denoising methods for astronomical surveys must be evaluated with photometric diagnostics, not image-quality metrics alone. With flux-aware modifications, self-supervised denoising can be adapted to low-SNR survey images while preserving the flux information needed for quantitative analysis.

papers.title: A pocket of oxygen in a near-pristine galaxy at z=4.2: chemical inhomogeneity at 10-parsec scales in LAP2
papers.abstract: We aim to constrain the oxygen abundance, the ionizing properties, and the spatial structure of LAP2, a strongly lensed (with a magnification $μ$~50) oxygen-deficient galaxy at z=4.2 behind the galaxy cluster Abell 2744. We present new JWST/NIRSpec IFU PRISM observations (~13.6 hr) of LAP2, which we combine with archival JWST/NIRCam imaging. LAP2 is intrinsically extremely faint (M_UV=-12.7) and has a low stellar mass (M~$10^5~M_\odot$), comparable to that of massive star clusters. It consists of a compact core ($R_{eff}$~7 pc) embedded in a more diffuse emission (with $R_{eff}$~20 pc). Strong H$α$ emission (EW$_{\rm rest}\simeq880$ Å, $\logξ_{\rm ion}\simeq25.3$), a blue UV slope ($β_{\rm UV}\simeq-2.5$, down to $\simeq-3.1$ in the core), and a Balmer decrement consistent with no dust attenuation indicate a young ($\lesssim10$ Myr), dust-free burst. [OIII]$λ$5007 is not detected in the integrated spectrum, implying [OIII]/H$β\leq0.61$ ($3σ$) and, using an extrapolated strong-line calibration, $12+\log({\rm O/H})\leq6.4$ ($\lesssim0.5\%\,Z_\odot$). This places LAP2 among the most metal-poor galaxies known. Faint [OIII] emission is, however, detected in the core (with $\rm4σ$ significance), where we derive $12+\log({\rm O/H})\simeq6.6$ ($\sim1\%\,Z_\odot$). This difference can be explained either by local self-enrichment, requiring only $\rm \sim0.2\,M_\odot$ of newly synthesized oxygen, or by a higher ionization parameter in the core. The upper limit on HeII$λ$1640 (EW$_{\rm rest}<39$ Å, $3σ$) does not exclude a contribution from metal-free stars. LAP2 extends the census of spectroscopically confirmed EMPGs to star-cluster masses and to $M_{\rm UV}\approx-13$. Its location in a low-density region supports a scenario in which underdense environments preserve nearly pristine gas well after reionization.

papers.title: Mock CSST NUV-NIR imaging of TNG50 galaxies with resolved stellar populations
papers.abstract: Aims. We aim to develop a framework for producing CSST-like mock images of resolved stellar populations from simulated galaxies, demonstrated here using two TNG50 galaxies as illustrative test cases. Methods. Starting from simulated galaxies from TNG50, we use the population synthesis code TRILEGAL to sample individual stars from star particles, retaining bright stars explicitly and treating the remaining unresolved light, including faint stellar light and nebular emission from star-forming regions, as a diffuse background component of the galaxy. Based on the dust distribution inferred from the gas mass and metallicity of gas cells, we use the radiative transfer (RT) code SKIRT to construct the dust model. From this model, we compute the line-of-sight extinction for individual stars, while image-level transmission maps for the diffuse light are derived through RT simulations. For young stars still embedded in their natal molecular clouds, we additionally include birth-cloud attenuation. The resulting dust-attenuated stellar catalogues and diffuse-light images are then processed with the CSST simulation pipeline, which applies PSF convolution, sky background, and instrumental noise. Results. Our framework produces mock CSST images for both a spiral galaxy and a dwarf irregular galaxy from TNG50 in the seven photometric bands. The mock images combine resolved stars, unresolved diffuse light, and dust attenuation within a unified framework, and include the main observational effects expected for the survey. The images are provided with known astrometric and photometric calibration information, and are intended as realistic image-level inputs for subsequent source detection, photometric recovery, and completeness analyses of resolved stellar populations. The framework is designed to be adaptable to other hydrodynamic simulations and observing configurations.

papers.title: The dwarf galaxy NGC 185: the flagship of Andromeda's dwarf galaxies for the study of evolved multiple stellar populations
papers.abstract: Reaching galaxies at 10-15 Mpc with HST and JWST requires star formation history (SFH) diagnostics that do not rely on the faint main sequence turn-off. We investigate whether horizontal branch (HB), red clump (RC), and red and asymptotic giant branch (RGB, AGB) stars can fill this role for dwarf elliptical galaxies, using NGC 185 as a test case. We use stellar evolution models of low- and intermediate-mass stars as inputs to population synthesis simulations that reproduce the colour distribution and luminosity function of stars in the (mF606W-mF814W, mF814W) diagram. The study of the stars populating the HB is used to derive the distance modulus and reddening, the average mass loss suffered by the stars during the ascending on the RGB and the SFH occurred during the ancient epochs, before 7 Gyr ago. The luminosity function of the RC gives us constraints on the recent SFH (<8 Gyr). The distribution of HB stars yields a reddening E(B-V)=0.20 mag and a distance modulus DM=24.10 mag for NGC 185. The average mass lost by low-mass stars during the RGB phase is 0.22 +- 0.01 Msun. Star formation was concentrated at early epochs, with half of the stars formed more than 11 Gyr ago. The morphology of the HB indicates essentially no metallicity spread among stars older than 8 Gyr, whereas the slope of the RGB suggests that part of the stars younger than 5-6 Gyr are slightly enriched in metals. Once RGB mass loss is adequately constrained, evolved stars can provide a reliable SFH for dwarf elliptical galaxies well beyond the reach of MSTO-based methods. We discuss the implications for more distant systems and the remaining uncertainties in the underlying stellar models.

papers.title: Tracking turbulence for wind-driven halo removal using MagAO-X pyramid wavefront sensor images
papers.abstract: The wind-driven halo (WDH) is a persistent, low spatial frequency noise artifact that arises due to the servo-lag error inherent to all adaptive optics (AO) instruments. Spatial filtering may be employed to overcome this artifact, however, filtering out the WDH while simultaneously preserving signal from an extended astrophysical object of interest is exceptionally challenging. Additionally, since the WDH changes in intensity and position angle through an observation, data-driven algorithms (e.g., KLIP) that are commonly used to subtract the starlight need to be overly-aggressive to remove both the static and dynamic noise components. Since wavefront sensors (WFSs) continuously track the closed-loop residual wavefront error, WFS telemetry presents the ideal resource for combating this type of noise artifact through postprocessing. Using archival WFS telemetry from MagAO-X, which is the "extreme" AO instrument for the 6.5-meter Magellan-Clay telescope, we demonstrate a novel workflow for WDH reconstruction and removal in individual coronagraphic science images. MagAO-X is equipped with a pyramid WFS capable of recording wavefront telemetry at a high-cadence which is saved during data acquisition. Given this, we detail how our WFS data processing pipeline, windsoCC, cross-correlates the recorded closed-loop wavefront to measure the wind vectors of several turbulent layers of the atmosphere above Las Campanas Observatory. We then make use of the wind parameters learned through windsoCC to reconstruct the WDH footprint by leveraging a parametric model. Notably, we demonstrate a dramatic improvement in object recovery using on-sky MagAO-X images of the disk around HR 4796A at visible wavelengths.

papers.title: Primary and Secondary Star Formation in the Spiral Waves of NGC 628
papers.abstract: To determine the role of spiral arms and stellar feedback on the formation of stars, we examine the positions of optically identified and emerging star clusters in NGC 628. We find that the youngest clusters extend further into the spiral arms at small radii than at large radii, as expected when the angular flow rate through a wave-like arm increases with greater distance from corotation. The embedded or emerging star clusters (eYSCs) are identified relative to four distinct morphological features in the 7.7 micron image: spiral arm filaments, spiral arm spurs, spiral interarm feathers, and bubbles. Spiral arm-related eYSCs are presumably first-generation stars made from interstellar gas that was directly compressed by the density wave, while clusters along the rims of bubbles are secondary generations produced by feedback compression. The mass functions of the first and second generations differ: eYSCs in spiral arm filaments extend to significantly higher masses than eYSCs in bubbles. Secondary star formation continues downstream from primary star formation, removing the expected age gradient through the arms. Bubble eYSCs account for approximately one-third of all the emerging cluster mass. The outer arms have a more mixed distribution of spiral- and bubble-related eYSCs than the inner arms, potentially providing a way to distinguish wave and material arms and to find corotation in wave-like arms. Among the 17 most massive clusters with log M(Msun)>4, eight of them are in four tight pairs; in at least one case, the dynamical time for the pair is comparable to the cluster ages.

papers.title: APOLLO-Timing: Annealed Phase - Orbit Lattice Linking across Observations for Binary Pulsar Timing
papers.abstract: Sparse observations of binary pulsars can leave the orbit and the pulse count across observing gaps uncertain. We present APOLLO-Timing, a Bayesian phase-orbit lattice method that fits timing parameters together with integer pulse offsets between observing sessions. PINT checks the candidate connections at fixed pulse numbers. For PSR J1912-1215, a preliminary Keplerian fit to variations in the apparent spin period and its derivative did not phase-connect 96 times of arrival (TOAs) spanning 1438.07 days in 23 sessions. Starting from its position, spin frequency F0, and first time derivative F1 estimated in that fit, with dispersion measure fixed, APOLLO-Timing recovers the orbit and a unique best-supported phase-connected solution without supplied orbital parameters. A repeat full-data blind search recovers the same pulse counts in 914.0 s, including the final fit. Setting the initial F1 to zero in the 17, 18, and 19 session subsets also recovers the reference path. The solution gives Pb = 17.526 days, x = 23.448 light-seconds, e = 2.65e-5, chi-square = 188.01, and a weighted rms residual of 5.08 microseconds. For a pulsar mass of 1.4 solar masses and inclination of 60 degrees, the inferred companion mass is 0.67 solar masses, favoring a CO/ONeMg white dwarf.

papers.title: Collective Characterization of Polar Crown Filament Eruptions
papers.abstract: Polar crown filaments (PCFs) are crucially related to the structure of solar polar magnetic fields. They are physically significant because of the ``rush-to-the-pole'' motion, which is an indicator of the poleward drift of magnetic fields from decayed active regions. The formation and evolution of PCFs offer important insights into the Sun's magnetic activity at high latitudes and the solar cycle variation. In this study, we present a collective analysis of 50 PCF disappearance events covering solar cycle 24 and 25. Among them, 24 show rotational motions, and nine have sufficiently clear magnetic configurations for comparison with numerical model predictions. In all nine events, the observed rotation directions agree with the model predictions, suggesting possible magnetic-flux-rope-like structures in these events. All except one of the PCFs in our sample disappeared through eruption rather than thermal disappearance, and most associated CMEs were slow ($<800$ km s$^{-1}$). For events accompanied by transient coronal holes, the estimated magnetic flux associated with the dimming regions is on the order of $10^{20}$--$10^{21}$ Mx. Time--distance analysis identifies 22 events with a clear slow-rise to fast-rise transition, with onset heights ranging from several tens to about 160 Mm and a mean onset velocity of about 2.8 km s$^{-1}$ after excluding the highest-velocity event. Together, these findings characterize the magnetic structure and dynamics of PCF eruptions.

background.title: Gaia DR3 Reveals the Kinematics of Young Stellar Objects in the Carina Nebula: Peripheral Expansion and Central Rotation
background.abstract: We investigate the kinematics of the Carina Nebula using a sample of young stellar objects (YSOs) cross-matched with Gaia DR3, together with $^{12}\mathrm{CO}\,(1\mbox{--}0)$ molecular gas observations and APOGEE radial-velocity data. The results show that the proper motions of the YSOs in the four peripheral subregions of Carina display a systematic outward expansion, and that the two-dimensional expansion velocities of the subregions are approximately $0.57\mbox{--}4.56~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. The YSOs in the Central Region exhibit ordered rotation around an axis at a position angle of $86.9\pm1.5^\circ$, with a rotation velocity of $1.75\pm0.03~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. Further momentum estimates suggest that the current expansion in the peripheral regions may result from the combined effects of feedback from massive OB stars and possible past supernova explosions. These results indicate that feedback from massive stars plays a dominant role in the dynamical evolution of the giant molecular cloud in the Carina Nebula.

background.title: Developing the Field Selector System for the SHARP Multi-IFU: Optomechanical Design and First Prototype Validation
background.abstract: This paper presents the innovative Field Selector System (FSS) developed for VESPER, the multi-Integral Field Unit of the SHARP near-infrared spectrograph. The proposed system employs an array of movable light-collection probes (Field Selectors) that travel along parallel, vertically offset planes to avoid mechanical interference and vignetting. The true novelty lies in its opto-mechanical synchronization: as each probe translates by Δy to select a target, a set of folding mirrors shifts by Δy/2. This maintains a constant optical path length, allowing multiple independently moving probes to share a single focal plane and form a continuous image on it, easy to slice by the slicer. A dedicated optical test setup was developed to characterize the positioning stability and repeatability of the probe motion. The measured mechanical errors were converted into equivalent optical tilts and incorporated into the SHARP optical model to assess their impact on instrument performance. The experimental results identified the dominant sources of positioning error and provided valuable insight into the relationship between mechanical tolerances and optical performance. The study also highlights several design improvements capable of significantly reducing probe tilting and enhancing system stability. The results demonstrate the viability of the proposed concept and indicate that, with the identified improvements, the system represents an excellent field-selection solution for SHARP and other multi-integral-field-unit (mIFU) spectrographs.

background.title: Orientation of the spin axes of large Kuiper belt bodies as an indicator of the mechanism of their origin
background.abstract: The paper analyses the orientation of the spin axes of Kuiper Belt (KB) bodies that have satellites. For most of these bodies, the axes orientations were estimated under the assumption that the orbital planes of the satellites lie close to the bodies' equatorial planes. It was found that the spin axes of large scattered disks and plutinos' bodies, including four dwarf planets, are inclined at relatively small angles to the planes of their heliocentric orbits. This feature points to a possibility that all the scattered disk bodies, together with the bodies in the 3:2 resonance with Neptune, originated from the disruption of a single large body. The origin of the bodies of the so-called cold component of the KB is believed to differ from that of the scattered disk. The orientation of the spin axes of these bodies may also provide further evidence supporting this distinction.

background.title: A Note On Lattice Definition of Gauge Theories With Chiral Fermions
background.abstract: Because of the fermion doubling problem, it has been a longstanding challenge to describe a lattice algorithm for studying four-dimensional gauge theories coupled to chiral fermions. Recently, an algorithm to do so has been described by Craig, extending partial results in the previous literature. Here we describe a variant of this algorithm, based on interpolating a lattice gauge field over the continuum (as in Craig's work) and coupling the interpolated gauge field to continuum chiral fermions. The same variant was also proposed recently by Hsu. In any dimension and for any anomaly-free representation, this approach can be implemented on a computer in principle, but not in practice by Monte Carlo methods because the chiral fermion path integral is not positive.

background.title: Magnetism among the oldest white dwarfs in the solar neighbourhood
background.abstract: We present a new circular polarisation survey of approximately 100 white dwarfs selected as featureless DC stars and combine our measurements with previous observations. Our compilation contains 205 objects, of which 24 show firm circular polarisation detections, while another four show marginal signals that require confirmation. Four magnetic white dwarfs originally classified as DC show polarisation spectra with significant contributions from spectral lines. Depending on the treatment of these objects and of the marginal detections, the inferred fraction of magnetic objects in the DC selected sample lies between approximately 10 and 14%. Among objects without identifiable line contributions, the circular polarisation never exceeds approximately 2%, substantially below the levels observed in some hotter magnetic white dwarfs with prominent spectral features. This is unlikely a symptom of field decay, since in our sample we find no significant evidence for a dependence of magnetic incidence on cooling age, and magnetic fields are detected in stars with cooling ages exceeding 9 Gyr. Instead, strong spectral line opacity provides a natural mechanism for producing much larger polarisation amplitudes than the continuum. In the full sample considered here, the incidence of detectable magnetism increases with stellar mass. Most average-mass magnetic stars for which repeated observations are available show no clear polarimetric variability, whereas variability appears more common among the most massive objects.

background.title: Object-independent evaluation of small-data astronomical image classifiers: architecture, representation, and acquisition shortcuts
background.abstract: Reported performance in small astronomical image datasets can reflect object reuse, field-of-view differences, acquisition settings, and catalogue-derived properties as well as astronomical morphology. We designed \dataset{} to measure these effects in a four-class task comprising galaxies, globular clusters, nebulae, and open clusters. The dataset contains 370 catalogue-supported physical objects, each represented by three Digitised Sky Survey FITS bands, and uses a group-constrained split of 222 training, 75 validation, and 73 test objects. We compared a custom CNN--Transformer trained from scratch with ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 under an adaptive full-field representation, a common angular field, and two central-region-masked controls, using three fixed seeds. In the one-pass object-independent test, mean balanced accuracy on the adaptive view was $0.773\pm0.014$, $0.874\pm0.054$, and $0.866\pm0.023$ for the custom model, ResNet-50, and ViT-B/16, respectively. No primary architecture contrast rejected its null after Holm correction; ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 differed by 0.007 balanced-accuracy points (95\% cluster-bootstrap interval $[-0.048,0.062]$). Controls based on acquisition and catalogue metadata reached 0.721--0.735, and central-region-masked adaptive views reached 0.731--0.800. These results demonstrate generalisation to unseen physical objects, but also show that image context, acquisition settings, and catalogue-derived object properties carry substantial class information. In this regime, high accuracy cannot be interpreted as evidence that a classifier learned target morphology, and the comparison does not isolate architecture from pretraining.
